info.title: Document Recognition API
info.description:
One cent per document, the same price at any volume, and charged only when a document is actually recognised: every response carries a `billed` flag, and `no_document_found`, `unreadable`, `unsupported_document` and `rejected` cost nothing. Every account gets 100 free documents every month, used before paid credits; after those, each recognised document costs one cent.

This document is generated from the Zod schemas in packages/contracts and the routes in apps/api (`pnpm generate`); it is the source of truth for the public API. Types, documentation, SDKs and contract tests are derived from it. Do not edit it by hand: change the schemas or routes and regenerate.

post.description: Runs recognition synchronously on one image and returns the extracted data. One credit is charged only when the scan is billable, drawn from the month's free credits first and from paid credits once those are used up. A scan is billable when the document type was determined and at least one of an MRZ with valid checksums, five or more visual-zone fields, or a decoded barcode was read. Sandbox keys are never charged: `sk_sandbox_public` recognizes the image it is sent, free, within its lifetime allowance, while a registered account's own `sk_sandbox_...` key is answered from a fixed synthetic specimen. The result is written down only when the retention window resolved for the request is above zero: `options.retain_hours` when the request names one, otherwise the account's own history-retention setting. Send `retain_hours: 0` to have nothing stored at all, so there is nothing to read back later. Besides an API key, this operation accepts a client token from `POST /v1/client-tokens`, so a browser or an app can send a scan without holding the key: the scan is billed and stored exactly as the issuing key's would be, and every request presented with the token spends one of its uses, whatever its outcome.

get.description: The account's scans, most recent first, as history rows, one page at a time. Only scans made with a live key and kept under a non-zero retention window are listed, and only while that window lasts; a sandbox key sees an empty list. `limit` sets the page size (1 to 100, default 100) and `cursor` continues from the `next_cursor` of the previous page, which is null on the last one. The full result of any one scan is read back through `GET /v1/scans/{id}`.

delete.description: Deletes a scan the account still holds, before its retention window would have ended: the stored result, its history row and its thumbnail. It cannot be undone – the scan can no longer be read, listed or replayed through an `Idempotency-Key`. The credit the scan drew is not returned, and the period's usage counters keep counting it. Only a live key deletes, and only its own account's scans; anything else – an unknown id, another account's scan, a scan whose window has passed, a sandbox key – is `404`.

get.summary: Balance and usage for the current period
get.description: The credits available to the key's account and the scans made in the current usage period, counted by status. The balance has two parts: the free credits, 100 every month, set back to 100 at 00:00 UTC on the first and drawn first, and the paid credits, which never reset. Every settled scan is counted, whether or not its result was stored, so the figures do not decay as retention windows pass. A key with no account behind it (the public sandbox key) reports a null balance and zero counters.

post.description: Issues a client token: a short-lived credential that can call `POST /v1/scans` and nothing else. Call it from your server with your API key and hand the token to a browser or an app, which then sends the scan straight to this API without ever holding the key. A token lives 300 seconds and allows 1 scan request unless the body asks otherwise; send `{}` to take the defaults. Its scans are billed and stored exactly as the issuing key's would be, a sandbox key issues sandbox tokens, and revoking or deleting the key ends every token it issued. The token is returned once and only its hash is kept.

bearerAuth.description: An API key: `sk_live_…` for an account, or the public `sk_sandbox_public` for trying the API for free, without registering. `POST /v1/scans` also accepts a client token (`ct_…`) issued by `POST /v1/client-tokens`.

image.description: The document image, base64-encoded (JPEG or PNG).

reference.description: Caller's own correlation string, echoed back in the response.

mode.description: Recognition mode. Only `full` exists so far.

expect_country.description: Country the caller expects the document to be from, or null for any.

date_format.description: Format of dates in the response. Only `iso` exists so far.

return_portrait.description: Whether to return the holder's photograph crop in `images.main_photo`.

retain_hours.description: How many hours the result stays readable through `GET /v1/scans/{id}`. `0` is zero retention: nothing is written down. Omit it, or send `null`, to use the account's own history-retention setting instead; an explicit value always wins over the setting. The maximum is 8760 hours (one year).

expires_in.description: Seconds until the token stops working: 10 to 900, 300 when omitted.

max_uses.description: How many scan requests the token may make: 1 to 10, 1 when omitted. Every request presented with the token uses one, whatever its outcome.

ClientTokenRequest.description: Optional limits for a new client token. An empty body takes the defaults.

fields.description: Every field the engine extracted off the printed document, re-keyed to our vocabulary – the open set. Always present; empty when nothing was extracted. A field read in more than one language appears once per language, so `name` repeats and only `id` is unique.

schema_version.description: The version of this body, always `1.0`. A consumer that pins this value checks that the body is the one it was written against.

billed.description: Whether this scan was charged to the balance.

confidence.description: How strongly the recognition backs this reading as a whole. Each entry of `fields` carries its own band as well, and they can differ from this one.

ScanId.description: Scan identifier: a UUID version 7 (RFC 9562), canonical lower-case `8-4-4-4-12`. Its leading 48 bits are the millisecond the scan was made, so ids sort in the order the scans happened – but treat the value as opaque: nothing else about it is part of the contract.

ScanStatus.description: Outcome of a scan. Exactly these five string values; there are no numeric codes.

ConfidenceBand.description: How strongly the recognition backs this value: `high`, `medium` or `low`. An unknown or missing probability reads as `low`.

upload_ms.description: From the request's headers reaching the server to its body being received and validated, with your key resolved and its rate limit checked. The allowance, idempotency and credit gates are claimed after this number is taken, so they are not in it. Dominated by your own connection and by how large the image is – this is the half you can shrink, by sending a smaller picture from closer by.

processing_ms.description: The recognition itself – the server-side engine call.

total_ms.description: From the request arriving to the result being complete. At least `upload_ms + processing_ms`; the remainder is the gates that run after `upload_ms` is taken – the allowance, the idempotency check and the credit hold – plus preparing the result images and mapping the engine's output into this body. It stops there: writing the history row and serializing the response happen after the number is fixed, so the same figure is stored and returned.

ScanTiming.description: The split of the request's time. Null on a scan made before the split existed and read back out of storage: only the engine call was timed then, and the two halves cannot be recovered from it.

country.description: The state that issued the document, ISO 3166-1 alpha-3. The same reading as `issuing_state` under the name most callers filter on; null when nothing was read.

country_name.description: The issuing state's name, as read from the document.

issuing_state.description: The issuing state, ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 – the same reading as `country`, under the name the machine-readable zone gives it.

type_name.description: The document type under its full name. Null on a scan read back from storage, which keeps no engine output.

type_confidence.description: How strongly the document-type match is backed.

number.description: The document number, as printed. Null when none was read. A series the document prints separately is in `series`, never folded into this value.

series.description: The document series, for a document that prints one as a field of its own. Null when the document carries none or none was read; it is never split out of `number`.

issue_date.description: The date the document was issued, ISO-8601 (`YYYY-MM-DD`). Null when none was read.

expiry_date.description: The date the document expires, ISO-8601 (`YYYY-MM-DD`). Null when none was read; `is_expired` and `days_remaining` are computed from it.

is_expired.description: Whether the document had already expired when the scan was made. Null when no expiry date was read, which is a different answer from `false`.

days_remaining.description: Days until expiry at the time of the scan; negative once expired.

given_names.description: The holder's given names, as printed. Null when none was read.

surname.description: The holder's surname, as printed. Null when none was read.

full_name.description: The holder's name as the document prints it in one combined field. Null when the document carries no such field – it is not composed from the two above.

birth_date.description: The holder's date of birth, ISO-8601 (`YYYY-MM-DD`). Null when none was read.

sex.description: The sex the document states: `M`, `F`, or `X` for unspecified. Null when none was read.

nationality.description: The holder's nationality, ISO 3166-1 alpha-3. Null when none was read; it is not assumed from the issuing state.

id.description: Identity of this entry, unique across `fields`: the key and the language identifier the value was read as, plus an occurrence counter when the same pair is reported twice. `name` is the semantic key and repeats – a document that carries a field in two scripts yields one entry per language – so use `id`, not `name`, to address or key a single entry.

value.description: The value of this reading: the national-script spelling on a national-script reading, the transliterated Latin value on the default reading (the one whose `id` carries the identifier `0`). Null when the field is empty.

language.description: The language this reading was made in, e.g. `Greek`. The default Latin-script reading – the document's own Latin page and the machine-readable zone, `id` suffix `@0` – is `English`. Null only on `days_to_expire`, a number computed from the expiry date rather than text read in any language.

FieldCategory.description: Which group of the report a field belongs to.

reason.description: One plain sentence naming what did not check out, for `failed`; null otherwise.
reason.example: Check digit failed for: document number, date of birth

lines.description: The zone's lines in order, exactly as read – two for a TD3 passport, three for a TD1 card. The zone's alphabet is `A-Z`, `0-9` and the filler `<`, so a line carries no whitespace. Null when the document carries none.

text.description: The same lines run together with nothing between them: one unbroken string, with no newlines and no spaces. Null when there are none.

MrzStatus.description: Verdict on the machine-readable zone: `passed` (present, every check digit valid and nothing contradicting the printed page), `failed` (present but something did not check out) or `absent` (the document carries none).

anyOf.description: Image as a `data:` URL with base64 payload.

document_crop.description: The document itself, cropped out of the uploaded picture and deskewed – the front side of a card, the data page of a booklet.

anyOf.description: Image as a `data:` URL with base64 payload.

rear.description: The reverse side of the document, when the picture carried one and a crop of it was produced.

anyOf.description: Image as a `data:` URL with base64 payload.

main_photo.description: The holder's photograph as printed on the document.

anyOf.description: Image as a `data:` URL with base64 payload.

signature.description: The holder's signature as printed on the document.

anyOf.description: Image as a `data:` URL with base64 payload.

watermark_face.description: The faint second copy of the holder's face printed into the page as a security feature – a different image from `main_photo`, and the one a verifier compares against it. Null when the document carries none.

anyOf.description: Image as a `data:` URL with base64 payload.

barcode.description: The barcode area of the document, when it carries one.

anyOf.description: Image as a `data:` URL with base64 payload.

chip.description: The chip area of the document, when it carries one.

ScanImages.description: Image crops, returned in the recognition response only. Each is scaled down by height, proportionally and never upwards, to at most 250 px for `document_crop` and 100 px for every other crop, then re-encoded with every metadata block dropped.

overall.description: Whether the uploaded picture was good enough to recognize from. `not_checked` when nothing measured it – a scan read back from storage, which keeps no engine output.
`not_checked` under the recognition-only scenario; populated by authenticity verification later.

checks.description: One entry per authenticity check that ran. Always present; empty under the recognition-only scenario, where nothing ran.

name.description: Our stable snake_case key for this check.

label.description: Our human label for this check.

detail.description: One plain sentence about what this check saw, or null when it has nothing to add.

docs_url.description: Documentation page for this error code.

request_id.description: Identifier of the failed request, for support.

event_id.description: Identifier of the recorded failure, when one was recorded. Present and non-null only for an unexpected failure the service reported to itself; quote it in a support request and it resolves to that one failure. `null` for every error the caller is meant to handle.

ErrorResponse.description: The single error shape of every error response.

ErrorCode.description: Machine-readable error code; each code has its own documentation page.

scans.description: The account's scans, most recent first.

next_cursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page: send it back as `cursor` to continue after the last row of this one. Null on the last page.

billed.description: Whether this scan was charged to the balance.

duration_ms.description: Server-side processing time of the scan in milliseconds.

deleted.description: Always true: the stored result is gone and cannot be read back.

balance_credits.description: Credits currently available to the account: this month's free credits plus the paid credits; null for a key with no account (the public sandbox key).

period.description: Bounds of the current usage period (UTC calendar month).

monthly_credits.description: Free credits the account is set back to at the start of each UTC calendar month: 100 every month.

resets_at.description: When the free credits are next set back to the monthly amount (00:00 UTC on the first of the next month); null when there is no next monthly amount.

free_allowance.description: This month's free credits, drawn before paid credits; null when the account may not draw free credits (its email address is not confirmed, or its free credits were withdrawn) and for a key with no account.

paid_balance_credits.description: Paid credits: bought or granted to the account, drawn once this month's free credits are used up, and never reset; null only for a key with no account (the public sandbox key).

credits_spent_by_kind.description: Credits charged within the period, by the kind that paid.

token.description: The client token. Send it as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` to `POST /v1/scans`. It is shown once and cannot be read back.

max_uses.description: How many scan requests the token may make.

sandbox.description: True when the token was issued with a sandbox key: its scans run in the sandbox, exactly as the key's would.

ClientToken.description: A short-lived token that can only run a scan.
